title: Engelbart pilot onboarding — Daniel Osei (pilot B)

google_calendar_event.summary: Engelbart pilot onboarding — Daniel Osei (pilot B)

notes_markdown:
### About Daniel

- Postdoc at CMU (HCII), works on accessibility of data visualizations; writes 2–3 papers/year with many co-authors
- Main tools: Notion (lab wiki + his own project pages, "everything goes in Notion"), Granola for all meetings, Zotero, Overleaf; uses ChatGPT occasionally, Claude rarely
- Paragraph he brought: grant-proposal "preliminary work" section

### Connect screen

- Looked for Notion first, then Granola — neither is there
- Clicked **"Other"** expecting a list of more integrations; landed on file upload and said "oh, this is just upload?" — confused for ~40 s
- Ended up exporting a Notion workspace zip (Markdown + CSV) and uploading it through Other
- Connected Zotero (~1,100 items) and ChatGPT export

### Import

- Notion zip: 318 pages imported as plain files; page hierarchy lost (folders flattened, database rows became separate CSVs)
- Notion file names carry the 32-char id suffix → titles look like "Meeting notes 3f2a…"; looks broken
- Zotero fine; ChatGPT 61 conversations, 0 skipped
- No Granola data at all — his meeting notes are where most decisions live

### Writing task

- First confirmed suggestion at ~9 min: a Notion page from a lab meeting (via the zip)
- Said the trail is "exactly what a grant reviewer asks — where did this come from"
- Wanted meeting notes as first-class sources: "half my ideas are said out loud"

### Daniel's asks

1. Native Notion connector (keep hierarchy, clean titles)
2. Granola import (notes + transcript)
3. Rename "Other"; show what's coming soon
4. Shared lab spaces eventually (not now)

### Action items

- [ ] Hudson — rename "Other" → "Upload files" + add "Request a source" tile (2 of 2 pilots confused)
- [ ] David — strip Notion id suffixes from titles; rebuild hierarchy from the zip paths
- [ ] David — scope Granola import (API / local cache) — this week
- [ ] Hudson — send Daniel summary + follow-up date

transcript.text: Hey, good morning — or, sorry, it's noon here. Good morning to you.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Good morning! Hi Daniel. Thanks for doing this.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Hi Daniel. Is it okay if we record? It's just for us.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Sure, yeah. I'm recording too, actually, in Granola. Force of habit.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Ha, so are we. Two Granolas.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Meta.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Okay, so, quickly, before anything, known gaps. Claude Projects come in as loose chats, no Google Drive, and dedupe is still early, though we fixed a bunch since Friday.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Okay. I don't really use Claude much, so that's fine.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Great. Can you give us the tour? Where does your work live?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Notion. Honestly, everything goes in Notion. Lab wiki, my project pages, reading notes, meeting notes. And Granola for all my meetings, which then I sometimes paste into Notion, sometimes not.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Mostly not?
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Mostly not. Zotero for references. Overleaf for papers. ChatGPT sometimes, for, like, rewriting an abstract.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: What are you working on right now?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: A grant proposal. Accessibility of data visualizations for blind and low-vision users. I brought the "preliminary work" section.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Perfect, that's a great test actually. Okay, let me send you the link.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Okay. Connect screen. Uh. Claude, ChatGPT, Zotero, Local PDFs... where's Notion?
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: We don't have Notion yet.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Oh. Granola?
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Also no.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Okay. So the two things I use most aren't here.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Yeah. I'm sorry. That's — that's useful to hear though.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: I'll try Other.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: [quietly] Here we go.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Oh. "Upload a zip or folder." Oh, this is just upload? I thought Other would be, like, a list of more integrations.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Yeah. That's — you're the second person to say that.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: It's a very "Other" thing to do.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: We're renaming it. This week.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Okay, well, Notion can export a zip. Should I just do that?
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: If you're okay with it, yeah. Markdown and CSV.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Give me a sec. Notion... settings... export. Okay, it's emailing me a link. Hold on.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Okay, got it. Uploading.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Can you do Zotero too, and ChatGPT if you have an export?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Zotero, yes. ChatGPT export, I have one from last month, sure.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Timestamp, import started.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Okay, it's going. Zotero's big, it's like eleven hundred items.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Zotero's usually fine. Notion's the one I'm nervous about.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Why?
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Because a Notion export is just a pile of files. We don't really understand it yet.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Ha. Okay. Done. Summary card. Notion — well, "Upload" — three hundred eighteen files. Zotero, fine. ChatGPT, sixty-one conversations.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Can you open one of the Notion ones?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Okay... "Meeting notes 3f2a" and then like thirty random characters. That's the title?
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Oh no. That's the Notion id in the filename.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: All of them have it. And they're all flat. My lab wiki had, like, a hierarchy. Projects, then meetings under projects. It's just all in one list now.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Yeah. The zip has folders, we're just ignoring them. That's fixable.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: And the database. My reading list database turned into, um, a CSV and then a separate file for every row.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Writing all of this.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Okay. This is really good. Painful, but good.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: It's fine, it's a pilot. Okay, what do I do now?
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Paste your preliminary-work paragraph into a page.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Pasted. Let me just, um, fix the end of it while it thinks.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Okay. Suggestions. Hmm. A Zotero paper, that's right, that's my own paper. And... this is a Notion page from lab meeting in May. "Meeting notes 3f2a" whatever.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Can you open it?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Oh, yes. This is where we decided to pivot from sonification to tactile charts. That's exactly the thing this paragraph is about.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Timestamp, confirmed suggestion.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: That's actually — okay, that's very good. That's exactly what a grant reviewer asks. Like, where did this come from, why did you pivot.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: That's the whole idea.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: But you see the problem. That decision was in a meeting. The Notion page is me pasting a little bit from Granola. The full version is in Granola. And you can't get Granola.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Right.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Half my ideas are said out loud. In meetings. If you don't have meetings you don't have half of me.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: That's — yeah. I really like that. "Half my ideas are said out loud."
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: You can use it.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: If we had to prioritize, what would you want first?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Notion, properly. With the hierarchy and normal titles. Then Granola, notes and transcript. Then rename Other, honestly, just say "coming soon: Notion, Granola," whatever. And then — someday — shared lab spaces. Not now.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: That's a great list. Thank you.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Can I keep using it? Even with the Notion mess?
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: Please. We'll fix the titles this week.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: I'll send you a summary today and a follow-up date.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Sounds good. Thanks, guys. This is genuinely interesting, I'm not just being nice.
transcript.speaker: Daniel Osei

transcript.text: That means a lot. Thank you, Daniel.
transcript.speaker: Me
